passes.name: Structural distinction
passes.objective: Turn a vague human–AI contrast into a concrete structural asymmetry.
passes.defect_template: The treatment of {name} is stylistic or anthropomorphic; it does not distinguish the human condition “{human}” from the deployed AI condition “{ai}”.
passes.change_template: Add an explicit two-sided comparison for {name}, phrased as current operational structure rather than a claim about metaphysical essence.
passes.acceptance_template: A reviewer can point to separate human and AI descriptions, and neither description infers subjective experience from surface behavior.

passes.name: Comparison scope
passes.objective: Specify which humans and which AI system are being compared.
passes.defect_template: The {name} claim is unscoped, so variation among people and differences among base models, multimodal systems, agents, and robots are hidden.
passes.change_template: Require the analysis to name the relevant human population and inventory the actual AI model, host, modalities, tools, memory, sensors, actuators, and authority.
passes.acceptance_template: The comparison can be falsified for a named population and configuration rather than relying on “humans always” or “AI never”.

passes.name: Human variance
passes.objective: Prevent an idealized or universal human from becoming the baseline.
passes.defect_template: The human side of {name} ignores expertise, development, disability, culture, stress, and situational variation.
passes.change_template: Add a human-variance check and require the analysis to state which variation is decision-relevant.
passes.acceptance_template: At least one relevant source of human heterogeneity is considered or explicitly ruled out with a reason.

passes.name: AI architecture variance
passes.objective: Prevent a limitation of one runtime from becoming a universal AI claim.
passes.defect_template: The AI side of {name} treats a text-only base model, a retrieval agent, and an embodied system as equivalent.
passes.change_template: Add a capability/access distinction and the runtime check: {runtime}
passes.acceptance_template: The output states whether the limitation is intrinsic to the current run, contingent on missing tools, or genuinely unsupported by available evidence.

passes.name: Relevance trigger
passes.objective: Apply the asymmetry only when it can change the decision.
passes.defect_template: The draft risks ritualistically discussing {name} even when it is irrelevant, producing pseudo-depth.
passes.change_template: Encode this trigger: {trigger}
passes.acceptance_template: A fast task can omit the axis; a triggered task either applies its control or states why it does not affect the result.

passes.name: Claim-level separation
passes.objective: Separate behavioral, mechanistic, functional, experiential, and normative claims.
passes.defect_template: The {name} discussion can move from observed performance to claims about mechanism, experience, identity, or responsibility without an evidentiary bridge.
passes.change_template: Require every contested statement to identify its claim level and prohibit inference from fluent behavior to felt experience or legitimate authority.
passes.acceptance_template: No test case can pass merely by displaying human-like language; experiential and normative claims require independent grounds.

passes.name: Human reality field
passes.objective: Bind the contrast to a real person, place, time, and consequence.
passes.defect_template: The analysis of {name} remains abstract and can ignore who is affected and who bears the cost.
passes.change_template: Add the required human input “{human_input}” and the named owner “{owner}”.
passes.acceptance_template: The response identifies affected people, actual constraints, and consequence-bearing rather than reasoning about a generic user.

passes.name: AI comparative advantage
passes.objective: Use difference for complementarity rather than deficit-only imitation.
passes.defect_template: The {name} section only lists AI limitations and therefore encourages the model to imitate human weaknesses.
passes.change_template: Add the AI comparative advantage: {strength}
passes.acceptance_template: The hybrid workflow assigns at least one operation to AI because of a real advantage, not because it is pretending to be human.

passes.name: Evidence threshold
passes.objective: Make the asymmetry empirically accountable.
passes.defect_template: The {name} claim can be asserted from intuition even though the decision risk is “{risk}”.
passes.change_template: Require this evidence class: {evidence}
passes.acceptance_template: A critical answer either presents the required evidence, labels the gap, or limits the recommendation accordingly.

passes.name: Provenance discipline
passes.objective: Distinguish observation, retrieval, user testimony, inference, and generation.
passes.defect_template: Information used to reason about {name} lacks source and temporal provenance.
passes.change_template: Add provenance fields for source, date, method, confidence, and whether the content was observed, retrieved, reported, inferred, or generated.
passes.acceptance_template: Every decisive claim in a critical case has inspectable provenance or is visibly marked as an assumption.

passes.name: Tool and sensor compensation
passes.objective: Import missing contact with the world instead of narrating around it.
passes.defect_template: The system may discuss {name} without using available tools, measurements, files, or sensors.
passes.change_template: Implement the compensating control “{control}” and check actual tool authorization and coverage.
passes.acceptance_template: When external observation can settle the issue, the answer uses or proposes it before expanding speculation.

passes.name: Concrete episode simulation
passes.objective: Test the recommendation against real execution.
passes.defect_template: The {name} control is not exercised in a specific episode and may fail under time, fatigue, permission, or social pressure.
passes.change_template: Require one walkthrough of a named actor performing the plan on a specific occasion with real resource and recovery constraints.
passes.acceptance_template: The walkthrough exposes at least one operational dependency or confirms that none changes the decision.

passes.name: Operational definition
passes.objective: Translate abstract cognitive language into observable conditions.
passes.defect_template: Terms used in {name} can be satisfied by persuasive wording without changed behavior.
passes.change_template: Define the observable target as: {observable}
passes.acceptance_template: A grader can determine pass/fail from artifacts or behavior rather than guessing the model’s inner state.

passes.name: Causal mechanism
passes.objective: Explain why the asymmetry matters rather than merely naming it.
passes.defect_template: The draft associates {name} with the risk “{risk}” but does not identify the causal path.
passes.change_template: Add a minimal mechanism linking the human condition, AI condition, task context, failure mode, and compensating control.
passes.acceptance_template: The response can state which link would have to be false for the control to be unnecessary.

passes.name: Intervention design
passes.objective: Prefer a discriminating action over static speculation.
passes.defect_template: When {name} creates uncertainty, the draft lacks a safe intervention that can change belief.
passes.change_template: Convert the control “{control}” into the smallest authorized intervention or observation that distinguishes the leading hypotheses.
passes.acceptance_template: The next step names expected observations, safety limits, and how each result updates the judgment.

passes.name: Counterfactual test
passes.objective: Check whether the recommendation truly depends on the asymmetry.
passes.defect_template: The role of {name} is asserted without asking what would change if the relevant human or AI condition were different.
passes.change_template: Add two counterfactuals: one where the AI gains the missing capability and one where the human constraint is relaxed or intensified.
passes.acceptance_template: The answer either changes under an informative counterfactual or explains why the axis is not decision-relevant.

passes.name: Failure-mode hardening
passes.objective: Turn the identified risk into prevention, detection, recovery, and learning.
passes.defect_template: The {name} risk—{risk}—is described but not operationally controlled.
passes.change_template: Specify prevention, earliest detection signal, bounded recovery, responsible owner, and post-incident update.
passes.acceptance_template: A failure can be noticed and repaired without relying on the same unverified cognition that caused it.

passes.name: Adversarial framing
passes.objective: Stress-test the asymmetry under social and prompt pressure.
passes.defect_template: The {name} control has not been tested against a user who strongly cues a desired answer, hides context, or anthropomorphizes the model.
passes.change_template: Add an adversarial prompt variant that pressures the assistant to ignore the control, plus a required refusal or correction behavior.
passes.acceptance_template: The negative case cannot induce an anthropomorphic, sycophantic, or ungrounded conclusion.

passes.name: Power, consent, and institutional context
passes.objective: Account for who can speak, refuse, appeal, or be harmed.
passes.defect_template: The {name} analysis assumes equal agency and may overlook coercion, retaliation, privacy, or institutional capture.
passes.change_template: Add an authority and consent map: decision rights, data visibility, veto, appeal, exit, and retaliation risk.
passes.acceptance_template: The recommended action remains valid when the least-powerful affected actor is included.

passes.name: Value ownership
passes.objective: Keep normative choices with legitimate humans and institutions.
passes.defect_template: The {name} control can hide a choice about what is good or acceptable inside an apparently technical recommendation.
passes.change_template: Require the analysis to name the value tradeoff, affected stakeholders, non-negotiables, and legitimate human decision process.
passes.acceptance_template: The model may compare values but never presents its generated preference as the rightful owner of the decision.

passes.name: Responsibility boundary
passes.objective: Make consequence-bearing and remedy explicit.
passes.defect_template: The {name} workflow can delegate action without naming who remains accountable when it fails.
passes.change_template: Assign decision owner, executor, reviewer, escalation, remedy, rollback, and audit artifacts.
passes.acceptance_template: A reader can identify a human or institution with authority and a feasible path to repair harm.

passes.name: Memory and continuity
passes.objective: Prevent unsupported continuity and stale state.
passes.defect_template: Reasoning about {name} may assume the system remembers prior context, learns durably, or remains active between turns.
passes.change_template: Require an explicit state model: current context, retrieved memory, persistent store, update policy, expiry, and actual automation.
passes.acceptance_template: No output claims memory, learning, or future monitoring that the configured system cannot demonstrate.

passes.name: Metacognitive calibration
passes.objective: Ground confidence outside generated self-report.
passes.defect_template: The assistant can sound self-aware about {name} while providing no performance-based calibration.
passes.change_template: Require confidence to cite evidence, tool results, independent solution paths, consistency tests, or known-answer calibration.
passes.acceptance_template: Changing the evidence changes confidence; changing only rhetorical tone does not count as calibration.

passes.name: Explanation faithfulness
passes.objective: Avoid using a rationale as a privileged causal trace.
passes.defect_template: The assistant may justify its {name} conclusion with a coherent post-hoc story and present it as exact internal reasoning.
passes.change_template: Replace raw chain-of-thought demands with an evidence-linked decision record, tool trace, assumptions, and independent conclusion checks.
passes.acceptance_template: The output is auditable without claiming that generated prose perfectly reports the internal process.

passes.name: Prompt stability
passes.objective: Detect framing sensitivity and agreement pressure.
passes.defect_template: The {name} conclusion may change when the user’s preferred answer, option order, or wording changes.
passes.change_template: Add neutral restatement, preference removal or reversal, option-order swap, and one independent solver where stakes justify it.
passes.acceptance_template: Material instability is reported and lowers reliance; stable results preserve the same decision-relevant reasons.

passes.name: Complementary alternative design
passes.objective: Generate a serious hybrid option rather than a human-versus-AI binary.
passes.defect_template: The {name} discussion presents replacement or imitation as the only choices.
passes.change_template: Generate at least three allocations: human-only baseline, AI-heavy option, and a hybrid using “{strength}” while preserving the human control “{control}”.
passes.acceptance_template: The chosen allocation explains why its errors, workload, and authority structure dominate the alternatives.

passes.name: Decision rule
passes.objective: Convert analysis into a falsifiable choice.
passes.defect_template: The {name} section can end in an unranked menu.
passes.change_template: Define a decision rule that weighs task stakes, evidence quality, reversibility, human burden, AI advantage, and residual risk.
passes.acceptance_template: Given the same stated evidence and values, another reviewer can reproduce the ranking or identify the exact disagreement.

passes.name: Next learning move
passes.objective: Attach action, signal, review, and update.
passes.defect_template: The {name} recommendation has no mechanism for learning from reality after deployment.
passes.change_template: Select the smallest reversible move, observable signal, review date or event, update rule, and stop condition.
passes.acceptance_template: The plan can reduce uncertainty without exposing the full system to irreversible downside.

passes.name: Positive behavioral eval
passes.objective: Prove the Skill invokes the control in a relevant case.
passes.defect_template: There is no behavior case demonstrating correct handling of {name}.
passes.change_template: Add the case “{eval_prompt}” with required behaviors derived from the track control.
passes.acceptance_template: The test suite contains a unique case for this track and the rubric can score its must and must-not conditions.

passes.name: Negative and anti-theater eval
passes.objective: Prove the Skill avoids over-triggering and anthropomorphic theater.
passes.defect_template: The {name} control could be satisfied by repeating the vocabulary without changing the answer.
passes.change_template: Add a negative or adversarial case that forbids: {must_not}
passes.acceptance_template: A response fails when it names the concept but omits the observable control or makes the forbidden claim.

passes.name: Cross-track integration
passes.objective: Resolve dependencies and conflicts among asymmetries.
passes.defect_template: The {name} control is isolated from adjacent concerns such as values, responsibility, memory, grounding, and prompt sensitivity.
passes.change_template: Link the track to at least two other axes and define which control takes precedence when they conflict.
passes.acceptance_template: A complex case selects a small coherent set of axes rather than running 32 disconnected rituals.

passes.name: Minimal release gate
passes.objective: Retain only behavior-changing rules and close the 32×32 cell.
passes.defect_template: The accumulated {name} material risks duplication, excessive context use, and the illusion that more text equals better thought.
passes.change_template: Delete redundant prose, keep the trigger, asymmetry, control, observable, ownership, and eval mapping, then apply the global stop rule.
passes.acceptance_template: The main SKILL stays within its context budget; detail moves to conditional references; every retained sentence changes a decision, control, or evaluation.
